soundness_flags.label: Definitions def:absolute-risk, def:root-mse-risk, def:probability-risk and the frontier theorems
soundness_flags.one_line: The infimum over T never states whether T may use the supplied public functions and radii, so the minimax experiment whose novelty is claimed is not formally distinguished from an ordinary sample-only minimax risk.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition prop:regular-benchmark-reduction
soundness_flags.one_line: For fixed n and r_{1n}, r_{1n}n^{-\kappa/[2(\kappa+1)]} converges to r_{1n}n^{-1/2}, not zero, so the displayed \kappa\to\infty reduction omits a surviving term unless an additional bounded-radius absorption convention is stated.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:four-channel-converse and thm:sharp-four-risk-frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The converse is conditional on ass:lower-shell-richness and ass:upper-shell-richness; arbitrary admissible shell constants are expressly outside the claimed lower frontier.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The four-channel frontier is sharp only over the reservoir-rich class \mathcal M_n with the two stated numerical shell-geometry restrictions.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 6.1, Theorems 6.1--6.2; Conclusion, p. 31 equivalent HTML lines 914--915
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves general structure-agnostic lower bounds and identifies extension beyond i.i.d. sampling, including distribution shift with weak overlap, as an open direction; its displayed covariate-shift experiment uses separate training and target samples.

The paper characterizes Gaussian and non-Gaussian IPW regimes under small probability weights, proposes bias-corrected robust inference, and selects trimming through an empirical asymptotic-MSE criterion.
The article links inverse-weight tail/support conditions to irregular identification and slower-than-parametric rates, including an exogenous-selection treatment-effect example.
